title: Optimal O(n(tau+1)) Vertex-Cover Sequential DP, Exact Signed-Rectangle Rank Sandwich, and Tight Triangular-Background Compression for Sparse Non-Monge Matrices
abstract: We advance the structural and algorithmic theory of matrices with sparse negative adjacent Monge differences (Delta C_{p,q} < 0), directly resolving Open Problem 3 and Appendix D questions of Chen (arXiv:2611.34733v1). First, a symmetric vertex-cover cut partition from a greedy 2-approximate vertex cover of the bipartite negative-support graph G_-(C) partitions {0,...,n} into m <= 2*tau(C)+1 intervals where every off-diagonal block and diagonal triangle is purely Monge; combining SMAWK off-diagonal with Wilber's doubling-phase algorithm (handling arbitrary base potentials) on diagonal triangles solves sequential 1D DP in deterministic O(s + n(tau(C)+1)) time with zero logarithmic factors, resolving Open Problem 3 in the vertex-cover regime and shaving Theta(log^3 n) off Chen Corollary 3.7 whenever tau(C)=O(1). Second, sharpening Chen Lemma 4.1 (s <= 2r) and answering Appendix D, we prove the exact signed-rectangle rank sandwich max(ceil(s(C)/2), max_p s_row(p), max_q s_col(q)) <= r_min(C) <= s(C) (tight at both r_min = s/2 and r_min = s) and an exact (n-2)^2 deterministic (Omega(n^2) randomized) entry-oracle lower bound for deciding s(C)=0 vs. s(C)<=2. Third, we sharpen Chen Theorem 5.1 using the minimal unit-curvature triangular background M_tri(k,j) = C(j-k,2) (Delta M_tri = 1) and tight multiplier lambda_tri = max(2, (a-1)(n-1)+1) = Theta(n^{1+alpha}) (saving Theta(n^{1-alpha}), >8x at a<=n/4), and compress Chen's n-leaf envelope tree to q <= min(n, 2r+1) elementary uniform-rectangle blocks (O(r) internal nodes) solving static min-plus matrix-vector products in O(n T_M log n + r log(r+2) log n (log n + T_M)), speeding up rectangle updates by Theta(log n / log(r+2)) over Chen Theorem 3.4. All 20 theorems are formally verified in constructive Lean 4.35.0 (0 sorry, 0 Classical.choice, 0 custom axioms) alongside 16 SHA-256 zero-float certificates and 56 adversarial tests.
